errors.text: The proposed 500–600 K hydride-decomposition step is not supported and is unlikely to fully decompose the Hf, Ti, Zr, Nb, and Ta hydrides sequentially.
The high-temperature condition is given as 1400–1500 K, far below the target 1400–1500 °C treatment needed for densification and phase stabilization.
The response replaces extrusion printing, hydrogen de-binding, prolonged vacuum sintering, and titanium-sponge oxygen gettering with pressure-assisted hot extrusion.
It seeks oxygen contents below 0.1 wt.%, whereas the target deliberately retains approximately 1 wt.% oxygen for interstitial strengthening.
It omits water quenching, the critical control that suppresses alpha-HCP formation and retains metastable single-phase beta-BCC.
Laves-phase dissolution is imported from chemically dissimilar CrMoNbWV evidence and is not established as the controlling mechanism in HfNbTaTiZr.
The predicted strengthening mechanism is internally inconsistent: the treatment is said to cause grain growth, while the outcome invokes grain refinement and precipitation strengthening.
